why: Both moved the same single call site with the same wrap and verified it live through on_message, so the deciding axis is system judgment, and B's is wider and sharper: a first-class `router` provider that turns llmcord's provider/model abstraction and /model menu into the Router catalog (with the correct caveat that Router has no /v1/chat/completions, so those entries 404 when the key is unset), the uncapped replayed history priced out as a ~625k-token, ~$3 worst-case turn, and replacing the VISION_MODEL_TAGS substring guess with catalog capability flags — three app-specific items A never raises. A is the better packager (it caught that the Dockerfile would ship an image without router_runtime.py and silently stop routing, and it documents the parameter-translation drops and the on/off switch for operators), but its improvement set is essentially a subset of B's with one extra split branch.
A_best: The operator-facing honesty on the migration itself: the README table of what routes and what doesn't, the exact carried/dropped/provider-pinned parameter sets read off the runtime's whitelist, the changed error shape, plus the Dockerfile fix that keeps a non-compose `docker build` from silently shipping a no-op runtime — and the per-channel-label footgun it declined to build because the label is also the policy key.
B_best: The `router` provider proposal (i4): it sees that llmcord is already organised around provider+model, that Router is that abstraction done once, that this collapses six vendor keys and makes /model the catalog — and it names the real cost correctly, that those entries lose the 'nothing changes until the key is set' property because Router has no chat/completions endpoint. The $3-per-turn history budget finding (i5) is a close second, and its Flex note (measured, already on Flex, left alone with the one-line reversal) is the right non-action.
A_worst: Enabling vision for the new default by writing the config key as `openai/gpt-6-luna:vision` — a model id with a suffix that only works if something downstream normalises it, rather than the plain fix of adding the `gpt-6` tag; it also never generalises that VISION_MODEL_TAGS will silently drop attachments for the next model family. Its fallback list (claude-sonnet-5-5 at $2/$10, then gpt-6-luna) is also stale against its own i4: once gpt-6-luna is the default, the primary is its own last fallback, and the first fallback is 20x the default's price.
B_worst: It ships the migration with no packaging or documentation work: the Dockerfile still copies only llmcord.py and config.yaml, so a plain `docker build` produces an image where the import falls back to a no-op and nothing routes, and there is no README line telling an operator how to turn routing on/off or which config.yaml model parameters survive the Responses translation. Four of its seven improvements are also unbuilt proposals.
